dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.pool.adjustHi: GM: click to give one back, right-click to spend one
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.category.togg: Click to fold this group away
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.font: Display face for the character name, pool headings and End Turn. Fantasy is Foundry's own Modesto Condensed; Clean is a condensed sans; System uses whatever your OS reads best.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.coupledPools: Only one of these two this turn
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.notify.noGM: A GM must be online for this.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.config.title: HUD configuration
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.config.notice: New suggestion from "{feature}": {count} attacks per Attack action (configured: {configured})
"{feature}" suggests {count} attacks per Attack action. Currently configured: {configured}.
{name}: staying at {configured} attacks per Attack action.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.config.attack: Detected automatically: {suggested}. Leave empty to keep following the detection.
Nothing detected automatically. Leave empty for {fallback} attack per action.
Leave empty to use the world default. Legendary actions come from the character sheet.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.acto: Attacks per action and pool sizes, per character. The GM can configure every character, players their own.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.maxB: Default pool size for bonus actions.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.maxR: Reactions refill at the start of the creature's own turn.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.enfo: How to react when a pool is empty.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.hide: Only show activities from equipped gear.
Cantrips and always-prepared spells stay visible.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.slot: How many rows of icons each pool stacks into. More rows makes the bar taller and narrower, fewer makes it flatter and wider.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.grou: Split each pool into Weapons, Spells (by level), Items and Features. Click a group's heading to fold it away.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.sort: Applies to entries you have not ordered by hand in the gear dialog; those keep their position.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.settings.scal: Size of the HUD on your screen.
Drag entries between zones to change which pool they use, or drag an item straight from the character sheet. Drag within a zone to set the order the bar shows.
Nothing here. Drop something to keep it off the bar.
Nothing here. Drop an entry to add it.
You are moving "{name}" to {target}, but it is detected as {detected}. Move it anyway?
Counts as one attack within the Attack action
Show or hide on the bar
Only features the bar shows as passive belong here.
That item belongs to a different character.
"{name}" has no usable activity, so there is nothing to put on the bar.
This feature is split across pools
"{name}" currently has buttons in more than one pool, because its activities disagree about what it costs. Move all of it to {target}, or only the group you dragged?
This feature has buttons in more than one pool. Drag one onto the other's zone to merge them.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.multiattack.n: Multiattack: the statblock reads {summary}. Nothing has answered for it yet.
This statblock reads: {summary}. One attacks-per-action number cannot express that. The editor opens prefilled with this reading — check it and save.
The statblock now reads: {summary}. That is not what is configured.
Silences this reading only. Re-stat the creature and the mark comes back on its own.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.multiattack.a: No Multiattack configured. The attacks-per-action number above applies.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.multiattack.h: Each alternative is one way to spend the Attack action; the creature takes exactly one of them. Several rows inside one alternative are combined. Nothing is asked at the table — using an attack simply rules out the alternatives it does not fit.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.multiattack.n: No alternatives yet. Add one, or take the suggestion from the statblock.
This creature has nothing in the Action pool that counts as an attack. Set that up in the HUD configuration first.
dnd5e-hud-to-rule-them-all.multiattack.s: Read from this creature's statblock. Nothing is stored yet — check it and press Save.
Reads the Multiattack text and turns each named attack into its own alternative. Check it — the text does not distinguish "and" from "or" reliably.
